summary: Defines an extension object that can be appended to certain ICMP messages so that Label Switching Routers can include MPLS information in them. This helps people diagnosing paths through MPLS networks see label details. The memo notes the extension was already widely deployed. It is on the standards track.

eli5.summary: When a mail carrier sends back a note saying a package got stuck, this lets the note also say which special sorting lane the package was in.

questions: how do routers report mpls labels in icmp
what is the icmp mpls extension
how does traceroute show mpls labels
what is the mpls label stack object
subtitle: How a router can tell you, inside an ICMP error, which MPLS labels your packet carried when it arrived.

tldr.problem: When an MPLS router drops a packet and sends back an ICMP error, the message says nothing about the MPLS label stack the packet arrived with, even though the router forwarded it based on that stack.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines an MPLS Label Stack Object that is appended to ICMP Time Exceeded and Destination Unreachable messages and carries the whole label stack exactly as it arrived at the router.
tldr.outcome: Traceroute tools can show the MPLS labels seen at each hop. The RFC is a Proposed Standard and notes the extension was already widely deployed.

today: RFC 4950 is a Proposed Standard and the metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. Its abstract says the extension had already been widely deployed.

sections.title: The Missing MPLS Information
sections.content:
Routers use ICMP (ICMPv4 and ICMPv6) to send control information back to the host that originated a datagram. When a router cannot deliver a datagram, the ICMP message says why, and includes the IP header and leading payload octets of the original datagram.

A Label Switching Router (LSR) that receives an undeliverable MPLS-encapsulated datagram removes the entire label stack, exposing the IP datagram inside, and hands that datagram to error processing. Any ICMP message that results contains no information about the label stack. That is a gap, because the LSR forwarded the packet based on that stack.

The general relationship between ICMP and MPLS is not defined here. It comes from Section 2.3 of RFC 3032.
sections.eli5: The router used a secret code on the package to decide where to send it, but when it reports a problem it forgets to mention the code. This RFC adds the code to the report.

sections.title: The Extension Approach
sections.content:
The memo defines an ICMP extension object that lets an LSR append MPLS information to ICMP messages. Selected ICMP messages SHOULD include the MPLS label stack as it arrived at the router sending the ICMP message. The message MUST also still include the IP header and leading payload octets of the original datagram.

The object must be preceded by an ICMP Extension Structure Header and an ICMP Object Header, both defined in RFC 4884. The extension applies equally to ICMPv4 (RFC 792) and ICMPv6 (RFC 4443). Here, ICMP means multi-part ICMP messages.
sections.eli5: The report keeps its usual details and gets an extra attachment with the labels. Both the old notes and the new attachment travel together.

sections.title: The MPLS Label Stack Object
sections.content:
The object can be appended to the ICMP Time Exceeded and Destination Unreachable messages. A single instance represents the entire label stack, formatted exactly as it was when it arrived at the LSR that sends the ICMP message.

The header values are Class-Num = 1 (MPLS Label Stack Class) and C-Type = 1 (Incoming MPLS Label Stack). The length is 4 + 4 * (number of MPLS label stack entries). Octets 0-3 of the payload hold the first stack entry, and each remaining entry takes another 4 octets in the same format.

Each entry has a 20-bit Label, a 3-bit Exp field (experimental use), a 1-bit S flag (bottom of stack) and an 8-bit TTL.
sections.eli5: Each label is a small four-part sticker. The object is just all the stickers the package had, in order, stuck onto the report.

sections.title: Enhanced Traceroute
sections.content:
The extension supports enhancements to TRACEROUTE. Enhanced implementations, like older ones, show which nodes the datagram visited on the way to its destination. They also show the datagram's MPLS encapsulation status as it arrived at each node.

The RFC's sample output (traceroute to 192.0.2.1, 30 hops max, 40 byte packets) lists four hops. Hops 2 and 3 each carry an extra line such as MPLS Label=100048 Exp=0 TTL=1 S=1.

The memo does not define encapsulation-specific TTL handling and defers to Section 5.4 of RFC 3034 and Section 10 of RFC 3035. When such procedures defeat basic traceroute, they also defeat enhanced traceroute.
sections.eli5: A traceroute is like checking each stop on a bus route. Now it can also tell you which special lane you were riding in at each stop.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The extension can give the user of traceroute additional information about the network, so an operator may want to share it selectively. The RFC suggests, for example, including the extension only in ICMP messages destined to addresses within the network management blocks that have administrative control over the router.

An implementation could decide based on the destination address of the ICMP message, on a global configuration option, or on the depth of the incoming label stack. An operator can also use the TTL treatment for MPLS Pipe Model LSPs from RFC 3443 for a TTL-transparent mode that prevents ICMP Time Exceeded altogether when tunneled over the LSP.
sections.eli5: Telling everyone how your lanes work may be more than you want to share, so a network owner can choose who gets to see the labels.

sections.title: IANA Registrations
sections.content:
IANA assigned Class-Num 1, the MPLS Label Stack Class, in the ICMP Extension Object registry. IANA also established a registry for the class sub-types (C-Types) of this class.

In that registry C-Type 0 is Reserved and C-Type 1 is Incoming MPLS Label Stack. The range 0x02-0xF6 is available for assignment and 0xF7-0xFF is reserved for private use. Values are assigned first-come-first-served under RFC 2434.
sections.eli5: A librarian keeps the official list of attachment types, and this RFC got the first slot for label stacks.
